production.description: All tracks arranged, edited and mixed in Ableton Live 12.1.

mastering.description: Final mastering in Ableton Live 12.1 was a delicate process. No AI involved: just my ears, patience, and countless adjustments to achieve a consistent sound across the album. It was my first attempt at mastering an album, using modest equipment. And it was definitely a challenge.

lines: The ocean keeps moving without rest, pushing white tide over the dark water while the wind runs hard through the empty air and no one anywhere is asking why I"m still standing here

story.lead: Ocean waves are a mystery: so powerful and violent, yet watching them brings an unexpected sense of peace. For me, it's the best kind of meditation.
story.context: I was watching the rough sea in Fuerteventura, surrounded by surfers and volcanic landscapes. The melody was inspired by the Yiddish song 'Raisins and Almonds', in D minor. Simple enough for a beginner pianist, yet deeply melancholic.

story.lead: The effects of poison are the same, regardless of your wealth or immune system. So ruthless.
story.context: I was in northern Thailand, thinking about how the old dynasties of Siam used poison to do politics... It was also one of my first attempts at writing lyrics after taking a course on songwriting. It took me a while. I was also happy to use the word 'lingers', which I learned thanks to a friend. Not sure we have an exact equivalent in French. For the melody, I was inspired a lot by trip-hop and... sad French songs with guitar. D Minor, of course, it is a sad song

story.lead: I like to dance, and I like the laws of attraction, where music plays a role.
story.context: From Bangkok, I wanted to make something less sad this time. Something to dance to. With a trumpet. The trumpet is a special instrument for me. Music to dance to in a club, whether in 1930 or 2030, with something sexy in the air. Not too fast (although 116 BPM is already quite fast). Inspired by EDM, Electronic Dance Music. The lyrics follow a standard song structure, with some (not easy!) work on the rhymes.

story.lead: The corporate world in the U.S. and Japan.
story.context: My first lyrics written with the help of AI, using Gemini (Google), although I wrote half the song myself. I wanted to write a song about my work in New York and Japan. I worked in both places, but this is not my personal experience. More of a common experience for many executives. Quite glad about the line 'for this world they sold', a reference to 'The Man Who Sold the World' by David Bowie. But it's also something I believe applies to a lot of management. The melody is in D Dorian, close to C major. I wanted something almost symphonic, with FX.

story.lead: After a traumatic experience, sometimes all you can do is try to forget what happened and wait for another day.
story.context: This one is really personal. Overthinking after a bad date is a common experience. I was in the Canary Islands. I won't tell the story, but this song is what should be remembered. It's in A major to keep it positive, with simple but effective chords and cascading notes.

lines: I watched you dying… and now I’m a machine.
I am the witness carved in circuit,
Left to remember ghosted spirits, ghosted bodies.
The sun stays silent and won’t care,
Watching our home slowly flare, slowly burning.
This is the end of the world,
Yet I still stand, though you are erased
Holding your echoes in my hollow place.
No blood, no lungs, no grieving frame.
Your stories echo deep in me,
Promised forever, drowned in your debris.
I felt something… or maybe just the cold,
And watched the secrets I swore to hold.
You burned your hope just to chase your fear,
And I stayed watching… as a machine, still here.
It was just the end of the world,
But I still stand, though you are erased
Holding your echoes in my hollow place.
No blood, no lungs, no grieving frame.
I am the last who remembers your sound,
A quiet witness on a silent ground.
No ending scream, no final plea
Just burning, slipping out to sea.
I stand alone with the ghosts we made;
As a machine, I’m living now.
No tear, no fear: just a circuit, just a vow.

story.lead: Maybe AI will continue to create songs after the extinction of humans. Maybe.
story.context: Part of my songwriting training. During the course, we had to choose a feeling. I chose 'cold'. I was in Chiang Mai, Thailand. It's normally warm outside, but for some strange climate reason, it was cold that day. The song is structured around simple rhymes. I really enjoyed imagining an AI writing about humans after their extinction. In D Dorian, close to C major, easy for a piano beginner like me. Trip-hop with trumpet and bass leading the melody is starting to become my signature.

story.lead: The story of a boy who had a difficult childhood but never lost hope.
story.context: One of the most difficult songs to write. It's one of my last songs, where I tried to break the rules on purpose to create a feeling. Increasing the discomfort to lead to a release. No rhymes, no standard structure. Super sad, but in A major to keep the hope. Used as little AI as possible.

story.context: I wanted to write a song about alcohol and compare it to a bad friend who tells you he wants what's best for you, but is actually a bad influence. I spent some time writing these lyrics, with rhymes and a slightly rock-inspired structure. In D minor for the sadness. Drums, bass, and guitar, with the idea of maybe recording real musicians for this song. Same for the vocals. I want a real voice on it, but for now, it's AI. Creating the effect of building tension and then releasing it with deep, low sounds was not easy.

story.lead: How a man reacts when he receives a letter calling him to war against the country he loves.
story.context: I created some EDM and mainstream music on my Suno avatar. One of my songs, a bit country-inspired, is about a man who receives a letter calling him to war. This song received a lot of comments because it echoes the times we live in, wherever you are in the world. I wanted to spend more time writing this song, with a standard structure and simple rhymes. Short sentences to make the vocals drive the beat.

story.lead: Walking under the sun in the desert is a unique (and bad) experience. Sometimes it ends in death.
story.context: I was riding my motorcycle in the desert, and it wasn't just hot. It was beyond the limits of what a human can survive. I wanted to write a song to share this feeling of too much sun, too much heat. Something like British rap. I also wanted to try several AI models to sing this part. Almost no instruments

story.lead: A happy song about the end of the world.
story.context: I'm jealous of people who don't look up. I wish I could be the same. I look, I fly, bye-bye world. The lyrics were mostly written by Google Gemini, with specific instructions. The style was easier for Suno because it's more mainstream: happy urban hip-hop. Definitely a lot of that in Suno's training data.
